records.question: By what means had God promised the gospel before Paul’s time?
records.answer: God had promised the gospel before by his prophets in the holy Scriptures.

records.question: According to the flesh, God’s Son was born out of which descendants?
records.answer: According to the flesh, God’s Son was born out of the descendants of David.

records.question: By what event was Jesus Christ declared to be the Son of God?
records.answer: Jesus Christ was declared to be the Son of God by the resurrection from the dead.

records.question: For what purpose did Paul receive grace and apostleship from Christ?
records.answer: Paul received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations.

records.question: For what does Paul thank God concerning the believers in Rome?
records.answer: Paul thanks God because their faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

records.question: Why does Paul desire to see the believers in Rome?
records.answer: Paul desires to see them in order to give them some spiritual gift in order to strengthen them.

records.question: Why had Paul been unable to visit the believers in Rome until now?
records.answer: Paul had been unable to visit because he was hindered until now.

records.question: What does Paul say the gospel is?
records.answer: Paul says the gospel is the power of God for salvation for every one who believes.

records.question: What scripture does Paul quote concerning how the righteous will live?
records.answer: Paul quotes the scripture, “The righteous will live by faith.”

records.question: What do the ungodly and unrighteous do even though that which is known about God is visible to them?
records.answer: The ungodly and unrighteous hold back the truth even though that which is known about God is visible to them.

records.question: How are the unseen things about God clearly visible?
records.answer: The unseen things about God are clearly visible through the created things.

records.question: What characteristics of God are clearly visible?
records.answer: God’s everlasting power and divine nature are clearly visible.

records.question: What happens to the thoughts and hearts of those who do not glorify God nor give him thanks?
records.answer: Those who do not glorify God nor give him thanks become foolish in their thoughts and their hearts are darkened.

records.question: What does God do to those who exchange his glory for the images of perishable men and animals?
records.answer: God gives them over to the lusts of their hearts for uncleanness, for their bodies to be dishonored among themselves.

records.question: For what dishonorable passions do these women and men burn in their lust?
records.answer: The women burn in their lust for one another, and the men burn in their lust for one another.

records.question: What does God do to those who do not approve of having him in their awareness?
records.answer: God gives them up to a disapproved mind, to do those things that are not proper.

records.question: What are some of the characteristics of those who have a depraved mind?
records.answer: Those who have a depraved mind are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and evil intentions.

records.question: What do those with a depraved mind understand about God’s requirements?
records.answer: Those with a depraved mind understand that those who practice such things are worthy of death.

records.question: Even though those with a depraved mind understand God’s requirements, what do they do anyway?
records.answer: They do unrighteous things anyway, and approve of those who practice them.

records.question: Why are some people without excuse in their judging?
records.answer: Some people are without excuse in their judging because what they judge in another they practice themselves.

records.question: How does God judge when he judges those who practice unrighteousness?
records.answer: God judges according to truth when he judges those who practice unrighteousness.

records.question: What are God’s patience, kindness, and goodness meant to do?
records.answer: God’s patience, kindness, and goodness are meant to lead a person to repentance.

records.question: What are those with hard, unrepentant hearts toward God storing up for themselves?
records.answer: Those with hard, unrepentant hearts are storing up for themselves wrath on the day of God’s righteous judgment.

records.question: What do those receive who have done consistent, good actions?
records.answer: Those who have done consistent, good actions will receive eternal life.

records.question: What do those receive who obey unrighteousness?
records.answer: Those who obey unrighteousness receive wrath and anger.

records.question: How does God show no partiality in his judgment between Jew and Greek?
records.answer: God shows no partiality, because those who sin, either Jew or Greek, will perish.

records.question: Who is justified before God?
records.answer: The doers of the law are justified before God.

records.question: How do Gentiles show that they do are a law to themselves?
records.answer: Gentiles show that they are a law to themselves when, by nature, they do the things of the Law.

records.question: Which sins does Paul mention that the Jewish teachers of the Law should stop doing?
records.answer: Paul mentions the sins of stealing, adultery, and the robbery of temples.

records.question: What challenge does Paul give to those Jews who rest upon the law and teach others?
records.answer: Paul challenges them that if they teach others the law, they should also teach themselves.

records.question: Why is the name of God dishonored among the Gentiles because of the Jewish teachers of the law?
records.answer: God’s name is being dishonored because the Jewish teachers of the law are transgressing the law.

records.question: How does Paul say a Jewish person’s circumcision can become uncircumcision?
records.answer: Paul says that a Jewish person’s circumcision can become uncircumcision if that person is a violator of the law.

records.question: How does Paul say that a Gentile person’s uncircumcision can be considered circumcision?
records.answer: Paul says that a Gentile person’s uncircumcision can be considered circumcision if that person keeps the requirements of the law.

records.question: Who does Paul say is a true Jew?
records.answer: Paul says that a true Jew is a Jew inwardly, with a circumcision of the heart.

records.question: From whom does a true Jew receive praise?
records.answer: A true Jew receives praise from God.

records.question: What is first of all among the advantages of the Jew?
records.answer: First of all among the advantages of the Jew is that they were entrusted with revelation from God.

records.question: Even though every man is a liar, what is God found to be?
records.answer: Even though every man is a liar, God is found to be true.

records.question: Because God is righteous, what is he able to do?
records.answer: Because God is righteous, he is able to judge the world.

records.question: What comes on those who say, “Let us do evil, that good may come”?
records.answer: Judgment comes on those who say, “Let us do evil, that good may come.”

records.question: What is written in the Scriptures about the righteousness of all, both Jews and Greeks?
records.answer: It is written that there is none righteous, not one.

records.question: According to what is written, who understands and seeks out God?
records.answer: According to what is written, none understands and none seeks out God.

records.question: Who will be justified by the works of the law?
records.answer: No flesh will be justified by the works of the law.

records.question: What comes through the law?
records.answer: The full awareness of sin comes through the law.

records.question: By what witnesses has a righteousness without the law now been made known?
records.answer: By the witnesses of the Law and the Prophets has a righteousness without the law now been made known.

records.question: What is the righteousness without the law that has now been made known?
records.answer: The righteousness without the law is the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all those who believe.

records.question: How is a person justified before God?
records.answer: A person is justified before God freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.

records.question: For what purpose did God provide Christ Jesus?
records.answer: God provided Christ Jesus as a propitiation through faith in his blood.

records.question: What did God show by all that happened through Jesus Christ?
records.answer: God showed that he is the one who justifies anyone because of faith in Jesus.

records.question: What role do the works of the law have in justification?
records.answer: A person is justified by faith totally apart from the works of the law.

records.question: How does God justify the circumcised Jew and the uncircumcised Gentile?
records.answer: God justifies both by faith.

records.question: What do we do with the law through faith?
records.answer: We uphold the law through faith.

records.question: What would have given Abraham reason to boast?
records.answer: Abraham would have had reason to boast if he had been justified by works.

records.question: What do the scriptures say about how Abraham was justified?
records.answer: The scripture says that Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.

records.question: What kind of people does God justify?
records.answer: God justifies the people who trust in him.

records.question: According to David, in what way is a man blessed by God?
records.answer: According to David, blessed is the man whose sins are forgiven and whose sins are not counted by the Lord.

records.question: Was Abraham’s faith counted as righteousness before or after he was circumcised?
records.answer: Abraham’s faith was counted as righteousness before he was circumcised.

records.question: Abraham is the father of which groups of people?
records.answer: Abraham is the father of all who believe, both the physically uncircumcised and the circumcised.

records.question: What promise was given to Abraham and his descendants through the righteousness of faith?
records.answer: It was promised to Abraham and his descendants that they would be heirs of the world.

records.question: What would be true if the promise to Abraham had come through the law?
records.answer: If the promise had come through the law, then faith would be empty and the promise not true.

records.question: For what reasons is the promise given by faith?
records.answer: The promise is given by faith so that it is by grace, and so that it is sure.

records.question: What two things does Paul say God does?
records.answer: Paul says that God gives life to the dead and calls things that do not exist into existence.

records.question: What outward circumstances made it difficult for Abraham to believe God’s promise that he would be the father of many nations?
records.answer: When God made the promise to Abraham, Abraham was about a hundred years old and Sarah’s womb was dead.

records.question: How did Abraham respond to God’s promise even with these outward circumstances?
records.answer: Abraham confidently trusted God and did not hesitate in unbelief.

records.question: How did Abraham respond to God’s promise even with these outward circumstances?
records.answer: Abraham confidently trusted God and did not hesitate in unbelief.

records.question: For whom was the account of Abraham written?
records.answer: The account of Abraham was written for his benefit and also for our benefit.

records.question: What do we believe God has done for us?
records.answer: We believe God has raised Jesus from the dead, who was delivered up for our sins and raised for our justification.

records.question: What do believers have because they are justified by faith?
records.answer: Because they are justified by faith, believers have peace with God through the Lord Jesus Christ.

records.question: What are three things that suffering produces?
records.answer: Suffering produces endurance, character, and hope.

records.question: How does God demonstrate his love toward us?
records.answer: God demonstrates his love toward us, because while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

records.question: Being justified by Christ’s blood, from what are believers saved?
records.answer: Being justified by Christ’s blood, believers are saved from the wrath of God.

records.question: What relationship do unbelievers have with God before they are reconciled to God through Jesus?
records.answer: Unbelievers are enemies of God before they are reconciled to God through Jesus.

records.question: What happened because of one man’s sin?
records.answer: Because of the sin of one man, sin entered into the world, death entered through sin, and death spread to all people.

records.question: Who was the one man through whom sin entered the world?
records.answer: Adam was the one man through whom sin entered the world.

records.question: How is God’s free gift different than Adam’s sins?
records.answer: By Adam’s sin many died, but the grace of God and his free gift through Christ abounds to many.

records.question: What resulted from Adam’s sin, and what resulted from God’s free gift?
records.answer: The judgment of condemnation resulted from Adam’s sin, but justification resulted from God’s free gift.

records.question: What ruled from Adam’s sin, and what ruled through God’s gift of righteousness?
records.answer: Death ruled from Adam’s sin, and those who receive God’s gift rule through the life of Jesus Christ.

records.question: What were many made through Adam’s disobedience, and what will many be made through the obedience of Christ?
records.answer: Many were made sinners through Adam’s disobedience, and many will be made righteous through the obedience of Christ.

records.question: Why did the law come in alongside?
records.answer: The law came alongside in order that the trespass might increase.

records.question: What abounded more than the trespass?
records.answer: God’s grace abounded more than the trespass.

records.question: Should believers continue in sin so that God’s grace may abound?
records.answer: May it never be.

records.question: Into what were people baptized who were baptized into Christ Jesus?
records.answer: People baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into Christ’s death.

records.question: What should believers do since Christ was raised from the dead?
records.answer: Believers should walk in newness of life.

records.question: In what two ways are believers united to Christ through baptism?
records.answer: Believers are united to Christ in his death and resurrection.

records.question: What was done for us so that we should no longer be slaves to sin?
records.answer: Our old man was crucified with Christ so that we should no longer be slaves to sin.

records.question: How do we know that death no longer rules over Christ?
records.answer: We know that death no longer rules over Christ because Christ has been raised from the dead.

records.question: How should a believer think of himself with respect to sin?
records.answer: A believer should think of himself as dead to sin.

records.question: For whom does a believer live his life?
records.answer: A believer lives his life for God.

records.question: How many times did Christ die to sin, and for how many people did he die?
records.answer: Christ died to sin once for all.

records.question: To whom should a believer present the members of his body, and for what purpose?
records.answer: A believer should present the members of his body to God as tools of righteousness.

records.question: What does a believer live under, which allows him to rule over sin?
records.answer: A believer lives under grace, which allows him to rule over sin.

records.question: What is the end result for a person who makes himself a servant of God?
records.answer: The end result of a person who makes himself a servant of God is righteousness.

records.question: Slaves of God have their fruit for what purpose?
records.answer: Slaves of God have their fruit for sanctification.

records.question: What is the wages of sin?
records.answer: The wages of sin is death.

records.question: What is the free gift of God?
records.answer: The free gift of God is eternal life.

records.question: How long does the law control a person?
records.answer: The law controls a person for as long as he lives.

records.question: How long is a married woman bound by the law of marriage?
records.answer: A married woman is bound by the law of marriage until her husband dies.

records.question: What may a woman do once she is free from the law of marriage?
records.answer: Once she is free from the law of marriage, a woman may marry another man.

records.question: How are believers made dead to the law?
records.answer: Believers are made dead to the law through the body of Christ.

records.question: Having been made dead to the law, what are believers able to do?
records.answer: Having been made dead to the law, believers are able to be joined to Christ.

records.question: What function does the law perform?
records.answer: The law makes sin known.

records.question: Is the law sin?
records.answer: No, the law is not sin.

records.question: What does sin do through the commandment of the law?
records.answer: Sin, through the commandment of the law, brings about every lust in a person.

records.question: Is the law holy?
records.answer: The law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

records.question: What does Paul say sin does to him?
records.answer: Paul says that sin, through the law, brings about death in him.

records.question: What causes Paul to agree with the law that the law is good?
records.answer: When Paul does that which he does not want, then he agrees with the law that the law is good.

records.question: What is causing him to do the things that Paul does, but does not wish to do?
records.answer: Sin that lives in Paul causes him to do the things that he does not wish to do.

records.question: What lives in Paul’s flesh?
records.answer: No good thing lives in Paul’s flesh.

records.question: What principle does Paul find at work in him?
records.answer: Paul finds the principle in him that he wants to do what is good, but evil is actually present in him.

records.question: What attitude does Paul’s inner man have toward the law of God?
records.answer: Paul’s inner man rejoices in the law of God.

records.question: What principle does Paul find active in the members of his body?
records.answer: In the members of his body, Paul finds the principle of sin taking him captive.

records.question: Who will deliver Paul from his body of death?
records.answer: Paul gives thanks to God for his deliverance through Jesus Christ.

records.question: What has made Paul free from the law of sin and death?
records.answer: The principle of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made Paul free from the law of sin and death.

records.question: Why was the law unable to set people free from the principle of sin and death?
records.answer: The law was unable because it was weak through the flesh.

records.question: Those who walk according to the Spirit set their minds on what?
records.answer: Those who walk according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.

records.question: What is the flesh’s relationship to God and the law?
records.answer: The flesh is hostile toward God and is not able to be subject to the law.

records.question: What are people lacking who do not belong to God?
records.answer: People who do not belong to God lack the Spirit of Christ living in them.

records.question: How does God give life to the believer’s mortal body?
records.answer: God gives life to the believer’s mortal body through his Spirit, who lives in the believer.

records.question: How are the sons of God led to live?
records.answer: The sons of God are led by the Spirit of God.

records.question: How is a believer included into God’s family?
records.answer: A believer is included into God’s family by adoption.

records.question: As children of God, what other benefit do believers receive in God’s family?
records.answer: As children of God, believers are also heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ.

records.question: Why are the sufferings of the present time to be endured by believers?
records.answer: The sufferings of the present time are to be endured so that believers may be glorified with Christ when the sons of God are revealed.

records.question: At the present time, under what kind of slavery is the creation?
records.answer: At the present time, the creation is under the slavery of decay.

records.question: Into what will the creation be delivered?
records.answer: The creation will be delivered into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

records.question: How are believers to wait for the redemption of the body?
records.answer: Believers are to wait with confidence and patience for the redemption of the body.

records.question: What does the Spirit himself do to help in the saints’ weakness?
records.answer: The Spirit himself intercedes in behalf of the saints according to the will of God.

records.question: How does God work all things together for those who love God and are called according to his purpose?
records.answer: God works all things together for good for those who love God and are called according to his purpose.

records.question: What is the destiny that God has predetermined for those whom he foreknew?
records.answer: God has predestined those whom he foreknew to be conformed to the image of his Son.

records.question: What else did God do for those he predestined?
records.answer: Those he predestined, God also called, justified, and glorified.

records.question: How do believers know that God will freely give them all things?
records.answer: Believers know that God will freely give them all things because God gave up his own Son on behalf of all believers.

records.question: What is Christ Jesus doing at the right hand of God?
records.answer: Christ Jesus is interceding on behalf of the saints at the right hand of God.

records.question: How are believers more than conquerors over tribulation, persecution, or even death?
records.answer: Believers are more than conquerors through the one who loved them.

records.question: What is Paul convinced that no created thing can do to the believer?
records.answer: Paul is convinced that no created thing can separate the believer from the love of God.

records.question: What would Paul be willing to do for the sake of his brothers according to the flesh, the Israelites?
records.answer: Paul would be willing to be cursed by God for the sake of his brothers.

records.question: What do the Israelites have in their history?
records.answer: The Israelites have adoption, the glory, the covenants, the law, the worship of God, and the promises.

records.question: What does Paul say is not true about everyone in Israel and all of Abraham’s descendants?
records.answer: Paul says that not everyone in Israel truly belongs to Israel, and not all of Abraham’s descendants are truly his children.

records.question: Who are not counted as the children of God?
records.answer: The children of the flesh are not counted as the children of God.

records.question: Who are counted as the children of God?
records.answer: The children of the promise are counted as the children of God.

records.question: What was the cause behind the statement given to Rebecca, “The older will serve the younger,” before her children were born?
records.answer: The purpose of God according to choice was the cause behind the statement given to Rebecca.

records.question: What is the cause behind God’s gifts of mercy and compassion?
records.answer: The cause behind God’s gifts of mercy and compassion is God’s choice.

records.question: What is not the cause behind God’s gifts of mercy and compassion?
records.answer: The cause behind God’s gifts of mercy and compassion is not the will or actions of the person receiving the gifts.

records.question: What is Paul’s reply to those who would question if God is righteous because he finds fault in men?
records.answer: Paul replies, “Who are you who answers against God?”

records.question: What did God do with those prepared for destruction?
records.answer: God endured with much patience those prepared for destruction.

records.question: What did God do with those prepared for glory?
records.answer: God made known to them the riches of his glory.

records.question: From which peoples has God called those on whom he is having mercy?
records.answer: God has called from both Jews and Gentiles those on whom he is having mercy.

records.question: From all the children of Israel, how many will be saved?
records.answer: From all the children of Israel, a remnant will be saved.

records.question: How did the Gentiles, who were not pursuing righteousness, attain it?
records.answer: The Gentiles attained it through the righteousness by faith.

records.question: Over what did the Israelites stumble?
records.answer: The Israelites stumbled over the stone of stumbling and the rock of offense.

records.question: Why did Israel, although pursuing a law of righteousness, not arrive at it?
records.answer: Israel did not arrive at it because they pursued it by works, and not by faith.

records.question: What happens to those who do not stumble, but believe?
records.answer: Those who do not stumble, but believe, will not be ashamed.

records.question: What is Paul’s desire for his brothers, the Israelites?
records.answer: Paul’s desire is for the Israelites’ salvation.

records.question: What are the Israelites seeking to establish?
records.answer: The Israelites are seeking to establish their own righteousness.

records.question: Of what do the Israelites not know?
records.answer: The Israelites do not know of God’s righteousness.

records.question: What has Christ done with respect to the law?
records.answer: Christ is the fulfillment of the law for righteousness for everyone who believes.

records.question: Where is the word of faith which Paul is proclaiming?
records.answer: The word of faith is near, in the mouth and in the heart.

records.question: What does Paul say a person does to be saved?
records.answer: Paul says a person must acknowledge with the mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in the heart that God raised him from the dead.

records.question: Everyone who does what will be saved?
records.answer: Everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.

records.question: What does Paul say is the series of steps which brings the good news to a person, so he can call on the name of the Lord?
records.answer: Paul says that first a preacher is sent and the good news is heard and believed so that a person can call on the name of the Lord.

records.question: What is heard which brings faith?
records.answer: The word of Christ is heard, which brings faith.

records.question: Did Israel hear the gospel?
records.answer: Yes, Israel heard the gospel.

records.question: How did God say he would provoke Israel to jealousy?
records.answer: God said he would provoke Israel to jealousy by appearing a nation that had not known him.

records.question: What did God find when he reached out to Israel?
records.answer: When God reached out to Israel, he found a disobedient and resistant people.

records.question: Has God then rejected the Israelites?
records.answer: May it never be!

records.question: Does Paul say if there are any faithful Israelites remaining, and if so, how have they been preserved?
records.answer: Paul says that there is a remnant remaining that has been preserved because of the choice of grace.

records.question: Who among the Israelites obtained salvation, and what happened to the rest?
records.answer: The chosen among the Israelites obtained salvation, and the rest were hardened.

records.question: What did the spirit of dullness given by God do to those who received it?
records.answer: The spirit of dullness made their eyes unable to see and their ears unable to hear.

records.question: What good has happened because of Israel’s refusal to receive the gospel?
records.answer: Salvation has come to the Gentiles.

records.question: What effect will the salvation of the Gentiles have on the Israelites?
records.answer: The salvation of the Gentiles will provoke the Israelites to jealousy.

records.question: In Paul’s analogy of the olive tree root and the wild branches, who is the root and who are the wild branches?
records.answer: The root is Israel, and the wild branches are the Gentiles.

records.question: What attitude does Paul say the wild branches must avoid?
records.answer: Paul says the wild branches must avoid the attitude of boasting over the natural branches that were broken off.

records.question: What warning does Paul give the wild branches?
records.answer: Paul warns the wild branches that if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare the wild branches if they fall into unbelief.

records.question: What can God do with natural branches if they do not continue in their unbelief?
records.answer: God can graft back into the olive tree natural branches that do not continue in their unbelief.

records.question: How long will the partial hardening of Israel last?
records.answer: The partial hardening of Israel will last until the completion of the Gentiles comes in.

records.question: Despite their disobedience, why do the Israelites continue to be loved by God?
records.answer: The Israelites continue to be loved by God because of the ancestors and because the call of God is unchangeable.

records.question: What have both Jew and Gentile been shown to be by God?
records.answer: Both Jew and Gentile have been shown to be disobedient.

records.question: What has God shown to the disobedient?
records.answer: God has shown mercy to the disobedient, both Jew and Gentile.

records.question: Who is able to search God’s judgments and give him advice?
records.answer: No person can search God’s judgments and give him advice.

records.question: What are the three ways all things are related to God?
records.answer: All things are from God, through God, and to God.

records.question: What is the spiritual service to God for a believer?
records.answer: A believer’s spiritual service is to present himself a living sacrifice to God.

records.question: What does a transformed mind in the believer enable him to do?
records.answer: A transformed mind enables a believer to know what is the good, acceptable, and perfect will of God.

records.question: How should a believer not think of himself?
records.answer: A believer should not think of himself more highly than he ought to think.

records.question: How are the many believers related to each other in Christ?
records.answer: The many believers are one body in Christ, and individually members of each other.

records.question: What should each believer do with the gifts God has given him?
records.answer: Each believer should exercise his gifts according to the proportion of his faith.

records.question: How should believers treat one another?
records.answer: Believers should be affectionate to one another and respect one another.

records.question: How should believers respond to the needs of the saints?
records.answer: Believers should share in the needs of the saints.

records.question: How should believers respond to those who persecute them?
records.answer: Believers should bless, and not curse, those who persecute them.

records.question: How should believers treat lowly people?
records.answer: Believers should accept lowly people.

records.question: As much as is possible, what should believers seek with all people?
records.answer: As much as is possible, believers should seek peace with all people.

records.question: Why should believers not avenge themselves?
records.answer: Believers should not avenge themselves, because vengeance belongs to the Lord.

records.question: How should believers overcome evil?
records.answer: Believers should overcome evil with good.

records.question: From where do earthly authorities get their authority?
records.answer: Earthly authorities are appointed by God and get their authority from God.

records.question: What will those receive who oppose the earthly authority?
records.answer: Those who oppose the earthly authority will receive judgment upon themselves.

records.question: What does Paul tell believers to do so that they can be unafraid of the ruling authority?
records.answer: Paul tells believers to do what is good so that they can be unafraid of the ruling authority.

records.question: What authority has God given rulers in order to suppress evil?
records.answer: God has given rulers the authority to carry the sword and to punish the one who does evil.

records.question: What authority has God given rulers regarding money?
records.answer: God has given rulers the authority to require payment of taxes.

records.question: What is the one thing Paul says believers should owe to others?
records.answer: Paul says that believers should owe love to others.

records.question: How does a believer fulfill the law?
records.answer: A believer fulfills the law by loving his neighbor.

records.question: Which commandments does Paul list as part of the law?
records.answer: Paul lists the commandments to not commit adultery, not kill, not steal, and not covet as part of the law.

records.question: How does a believer fulfill the law?
records.answer: A believer fulfills the law by loving his neighbor.

records.question: What does Paul say believers should put aside, and put on?
records.answer: Paul says believers should put aside the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.

records.question: In what activities are believers not to walk?
records.answer: Believers are not to walk in wild celebrations, drunkenness, sexual immorality, uncontrolled lust, strife, or jealousy.

records.question: What should be the believer’s attitude toward the lusts of the flesh?
records.answer: The believer should make no provision for the lusts of the flesh.

records.question: What kind of food does a person with stronger faith eat, and what does a person with weaker faith eat?
records.answer: A person who is stronger in faith eats anything, but a person who is weaker in faith eats only vegetables.

records.question: Who has received both the one who eats anything and the one who eats only vegetables?
records.answer: God has received both the one who eats anything and the one who eats only vegetables.

records.question: What attitude should believers who differ on what they eat have toward one another?
records.answer: Believers who differ on what they eat should not despise or judge each other.

records.question: What other issue does Paul mention as being an issue of personal conviction?
records.answer: Paul mentions as an issue of personal conviction whether one day is valued over another or all days are valued equally.

records.question: For what do believers live and die?
records.answer: Believers live and die for the Lord.

records.question: Where will all believers ultimately stand?
records.answer: All believers will ultimately stand before the judgment seat of God.

records.question: What attitude should a brother have toward another brother on issues of personal conviction?
records.answer: A brother should not place a stumbling block or a snare for another brother on issues of personal conviction.

records.question: Paul is persuaded in the Lord Jesus that which foods are unclean?
records.answer: Paul is persuaded that no foods are unclean.

records.question: About what is the kingdom of God?
records.answer: The kingdom of God is about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

records.question: What does Paul say a brother should do in the presence of another brother who does not eat meat or drink wine?
records.answer: Paul says it is good if the brother does not eat meat or drink wine in the presence of the other brother.

records.question: What is the result if a person does not act from faith?
records.answer: Whatever actions are not taken from faith are sin.

records.question: What attitude should believers with strong faith have toward those with weak faith?
records.answer: Believers with strong faith should bear the weaknesses of those with weak faith, in order to build them up.

records.question: Who is the example Paul uses of one who did not live to please himself, but served others?
records.answer: Christ did not live to please himself, but served others.

records.question: What was one of the purposes of the Scriptures written previously?
records.answer: The Scriptures written previously were written for our instruction.

records.question: What does Paul desire for the believers through their exercise of patience and encouragement with each other?
records.answer: Paul desires that the believers be of the same mind with each other.

records.question: Who is the example Paul uses of one who lived to serve others?
records.answer: Christ lived to served others.

records.question: What do the scriptures say the Gentiles will do because of God’s mercy toward them?
records.answer: The scriptures say the Gentiles will rejoice and praise the Lord.

records.question: What does Paul say the believers will be able to do by the power of the Holy Spirit?
records.answer: The believers will be filled with joy and peace, and will abound in hope.

records.question: What gift did God give Paul, which is Paul’s mission?
records.answer: Paul’s mission is to be a servant of Christ Jesus sent to the Gentiles.

records.question: By what means has Christ worked through Paul to bring about the obedience of the Gentiles?
records.answer: Christ has worked through Paul by word and action, by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Holy Spirit.

records.question: Where does Paul desire to proclaim the gospel?
records.answer: Paul desires to proclaim the gospel where Christ is not known by name.

records.question: Where does Paul plan to travel that will also allow him to come to Rome?
records.answer: Paul plans to travel to Spain, which will also allow him to come to Rome.

records.question: Why is Paul now going to Jerusalem?
records.answer: Paul is now going to Jerusalem to serve the believers there.

records.question: Why does Paul say the Gentile believers owe the Jewish believers material things?
records.answer: The Gentiles believers owe the Jewish believers material things because the Gentile believers have shared in the spiritual things of the Jewish believers.

records.question: From whom does Paul wish to be delivered?
records.answer: Paul wishes to be delivered from those who are disobedient in Judea.

records.question: What has sister Phoebe become to Paul?
records.answer: Sister Phoebe has become a helper of Paul and of many others.

records.question: What have Prisca and Aquila done for Paul in the past?
records.answer: Prisca and Aquila have risked their lives for Paul in the past.

records.question: Where is one place the believers are meeting in Rome?
records.answer: The believers in Rome are meeting in the house of Prisca and Aquila.

records.question: What experience have Andronicus and Junias shared with Paul in the past?
records.answer: Andronicus and Junias have been fellow prisoners with Paul in the past.

records.question: How do the believers greet one another?
records.answer: The believers greet one another with a holy kiss.

records.question: What are some doing, which is causing divisions and stumbling?
records.answer: Some are going beyond the teaching they have learned, deceiving the hearts of the innocent.

records.question: What does Paul tell the believers to do with those causing divisions and stumbling?
records.answer: Paul tells the believers to turn away from those causing divisions and stumbling.

records.question: What attitude does Paul want the believers to have toward good and evil?
records.answer: Paul wants the believers to be wise to that which is good, and innocent to that which is evil.

records.question: What will the God of peace be doing soon?
records.answer: The God of peace will soon be crushing Satan under the believers’ feet.

records.question: Who actually wrote down this epistle?
records.answer: Tertius actually wrote down this epistle.

records.question: What occupation does the believer Erastus have?
records.answer: Erastus is the treasurer of the city.

records.question: What revelation that had been kept secret from long ago is Paul now preaching?
records.answer: Paul is now preaching the revelation of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

records.question: For what purpose is Paul preaching?
records.answer: Paul is preaching for the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles.
